newsitem.title: UK: Fewer UK managers support Conservatives - survey.
newsitem.headline: Fewer UK managers support Conservatives - survey.

text.p: Fewer British managers support the ruling Conservative Party now than at the time of the last general election in 1992, an Institute of Management survey released on Monday showed.
Only 42 percent of managers back the Conservatives now, compared with 62 percent at the last election.
Support for the opposition Labour Party has jumped 13 percent to 25 percent.
The survey also showed more than a third of UK managers feel insecure in their jobs.
A majority, 59 percent, do not think they will become financially better off in the next year although 54 percent expect the UK economy to improve over the next 12 months.
"Managers are bullish about the prospects for business growth," said Roger Young, the Institute's director-general.
"However, they are sceptical about growth feeding through to personal well-being. Job insecurity continues to dog British managers and snap at the heels of the government's electoral fortunes."
The survey received responses from 400 managers.
